item.text: {"question_id":"5B.7","answer":"During 2023, the state made some economic and administrative information publicly available: a budget-law record was published, the government had a framework for publishing state-enterprise accounts and procurement contracts under the IMF program, and the NTRA fined Telecom Egypt after a service failure (BATCH-0013-E001; BATCH-0022-E014; BATCH-0002-E035). The government also reported disciplinary measures and created monitoring provisions in the responsible-AI charter, but these are indirect or self-reported evidence and do not establish independent economic evaluation or effective correction (BATCH-0023-E014; BATCH-0020-E001; BATCH-0020-E002). The evidence is materially adverse: state-owned-enterprise debt remained inaccessible, military-enterprise allocations were omitted from budget documents, and audits of large SOEs were not public (BATCH-0002-E005). Military-managed project and environmental data were largely inaccessible, independent verification was obstructed, and the government's 2022 transparency pledge had no documented completed disclosures or audits by the end of 2023 (BATCH-0009-R10-E004; BATCH-0009-R10-E017). Strategy documents were criticized for lacking implementation, monitoring, follow-up, and mechanisms to identify weaknesses, while official claims about reform success were not independently verified (BATCH-0009-R10-E003; BATCH-0003-E012). Parliament's listing of audit reports for fiscal year 2022–2023, published in August 2024, confirms report availability but supplies no findings or evidence of corrective action during the target period (BATCH-0003-E002). Overall, the record supports selective reporting and limited enforcement, but not reliable, independently testable economic information or a demonstrated pattern of evidence-led correction.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0013-E001","BATCH-0022-E014","BATCH-0002-E035","BATCH-0023-E014","BATCH-0020-E001","BATCH-0020-E002","BATCH-0003-E002"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0002-E005","BATCH-0009-R10-E004","BATCH-0009-R10-E017","BATCH-0009-R10-E003","BATCH-0003-E012"],"limitations_and_gaps":["The supplied evidence does not show complete economic audit findings, independently verified evaluations, or a documented economic policy reversal tied to demonstrated failure.","Several favorable items are plans, framework commitments, institutional rules, or government reports rather than evidence of implementation and outcomes.","The 2024 publication of fiscal-year 2022–2023 audit-report listings extends beyond the target period and provides no findings."],"corrections_made":["Removed the Patrick Zaki pardon and Sinai counterterrorism shift as irrelevant to this economic-information and correction question.","Recast the Interior Ministry disciplinary figures as self-reported, non-economic, and insufficient to establish effective correction or deterrence.","Added the omitted military-enterprise debt and allocations, inaccessible SOE audits, inaccessible project data, and undocumented implementation of transparency pledges.","Qualified the budget record, AI charter, IMF commitments, and audit listings as publication or framework evidence rather than proof of reliable information, independent evaluation, or corrective action."],"reasons_to_reopen_full_ledger":["A fuller ledger would be needed to identify completed economic audits, independent evaluations, verified fiscal disclosures, or documented policy corrections within 2023."]}
